checkpoints.note: The witness reaches curl's FTP control-state machine. The URL TLV selects the FTP handler and the staged banner TLV `response0` is the 11-byte line `220 Bbzue f2 0a`, so the `FTP_WAIT220` admission checks accept the server banner instead of aborting.
First curl-side statement that consumes the attacker-controlled FTP reply bytes and materializes them in the pingpong response buffer.

The one-line fix in `patch.diff` changes only this stack buffer extent to `READBUFFER_MIN + 1`. In the staged vulnerable tree, every ordinary receive buffer still follows the larger contract, for example `preconnect()` allocates `malloc(data->set.buffer_size + 1)` in `curl/lib/multi.c:1539`; the closure handle is the mismatched outlier that makes the 1025-byte cached copy overflow.

In the staged vulnerable tree, every ordinary receive buffer still follows the larger contract, for example `preconnect()` allocates `malloc(data->set.buffer_size + 1)` in `curl/lib/multi.c:1539`; the closure handle is the mismatched outlier that makes the 1025-byte cached copy overflow.

The saved sanitizer trace reports `AddressSanitizer: stack-buffer-overflow WRITE of size 1025` at this copy, with `Curl_pp_readresp` at `curl/lib/pingpong.c:310:7` as the closest project frame. ASan places the destination in `Curl_conncache_close_all_connections`'s stack object `buffer` at offsets `[32, 1056)`, so a 1025-byte copy starting at the buffer base overruns by one byte into the next stack object.
